drugs.justification: Satisfies L1 robust proximity, L2 binding to a module protein, L3 literature rationale; does not satisfy none; PRISM: no association with checkpoint strength. Its proximity comes only from membership of generic complexes (proteasome or tubulin): it disappears when they are removed from the modules. Broad target profile: closeness may reflect breadth.
drugs.name: BORTEZOMIB

repositioning.caveat: The support is from yeast and cancer cells and no paper on proteasome inhibitors in BUB1B-deficient cells was verified. In cell lines there is no association with checkpoint strength before adjusting; after adjusting for proliferation the direction is the same as for microtubule agents (less effective with a weak checkpoint). The network proximity of this class is membership of the proteasome in the checkpoint pathways, so it is not independent evidence.
repositioning.new_use: Tumour-directed: proteasome inhibition to exploit the proteotoxic stress of aneuploid cells, if the child develops a tumour (rhabdomyosarcoma or Wilms tumour are the tumours reported in this syndrome). It does not treat the constitutional defect.
repositioning.validation: Dose-response of a proteasome inhibitor in patient-derived cells or BUB1B-hypomorphic engineered cells against isogenic controls; read-outs: selective killing of aneuploid cells (karyotype or single-cell sequencing) and proteotoxic stress markers (ubiquitinated proteins, HSP70). Refuted if aneuploid and diploid cells are equally sensitive.

repositioning.caveat: Antimitotic payloads depend on the spindle checkpoint: cell-line data and taxane studies point to less effect where the checkpoint is weak.
repositioning.new_use: Tumour-directed delivery of a tubulin toxin to cells that carry CD30 (TNFRSF8): relevant only if the child's tumour expresses that antigen (not established for any tumour of this syndrome). The payload is an antimitotic.
repositioning.validation: Immunohistochemistry for the antigen in the child's tumour or in rhabdomyosarcoma and Wilms tumour models. Refuted if the antigen is absent; and test the payload in BUB1B-hypomorphic cells, where less effect is expected.

repositioning.caveat: A broad binder: closeness to the module may reflect breadth of targets and not specificity.
repositioning.new_use: Hypothesis that it acts on the checkpoint and mitotic network, because it binds NEK9, PLK4, AURKA (measured activity at or below 1 uM), proteins of or next to the modules; this would act on consequence 1. The direction of effect is unknown.
repositioning.validation: Confirm binding with an orthogonal assay (biochemical kinase assay, thermal shift) at relevant concentrations and test mitotic fidelity (mitotic index, micronuclei, lagging chromosomes) in cells. Refuted if there is no engagement or no effect.

repositioning.caveat: No drug was tested in those mice and the drugs carry boxed warnings; in cell lines the weak-checkpoint group is not more sensitive (an apparent resistance of sirolimus disappears after adjusting for proliferation).
repositioning.new_use: For the growth restriction, muscle atrophy and senescence consequences: BubR1-mutant mice show sarcopenia that correlates with mTORC1 hyperactivity, and the proband has short stature and muscle atrophy. An extrapolation from mouse genetics.
repositioning.validation: mTORC1 activity (phospho-S6) and muscle-differentiation or growth phenotypes in patient-derived myoblasts or in the BubR1 hypomorphic mouse model. Refuted if mTORC1 is not raised or the drug does not change the phenotype.
